{{No footnotes|date=June 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''Ringel–Hall algebra''' is a generalization of the [[Hall algebra]], studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Ringel | first=Claus Michael | author-link=Claus Michael Ringel|year=1990}}. It has a basis of equivalence classes of objects of an [[abelian category]], and the structure constants for this basis are related to the numbers of extensions of objects in the category.
